title: C++ language & STL
description: C++-specific mechanics. Kept separate from concept nodes so 'understands the idea' and 'can write it in C++' are graded independently.

nodes.name: std::vector essentials
nodes.description: Sizing, push_back, size(), back(), unchecked operator[], contiguous storage, cost of erase/insert.

facets.explain: Knows push_back is amortized O(1), erase/insert in the middle is O(n), operator[] does no bounds check.
facets.implement: Sizes before indexing (vector<int> v(n, 0)) or uses push_back; uses back()/front() only on non-empty vectors.

misconceptions.desc: Assigned v[i] on an empty vector instead of sizing it or using push_back.
signals: Runtime Error with empty output vector

misconceptions.desc: Called erase() inside a loop: O(n) per call gives O(n²), and indices shift under the loop.
Called back()/front() or [0] on an empty vector.
signals: if (res.back() != x) with res possibly empty

nodes.name: Pass by value vs reference
nodes.description: vector<int> copies, vector<int>& aliases the caller's object, const vector<int>& avoids copies for read-only access.

facets.explain: Knows what is copied when, and how copies affect time/memory (especially in recursion).
facets.implement: Uses & for in-place problems and const& for read-only parameters.

misconceptions.desc: Took the vector by value in an in-place helper, so the caller never sees the change.
Passed large vectors by value in a loop or recursion, causing O(n) copies per call (TLE/MLE).

nodes.name: Integer types & overflow
nodes.description: int vs long long, where values exceed 2^31-1, and conversion happening after overflow.

facets.recognize: Spots where values can exceed INT_MAX (~2.1e9): sums of many large values, products, nCr, pair counts up to n²/2.
facets.explain: Knows signed overflow is undefined behaviour and that a*b is computed in int before assignment.
facets.implement: Uses long long and 1LL * / (long long) casts before the operation that would overflow.

misconceptions.desc: Accumulated a sum or count in int where it can exceed INT_MAX.
signals: int sum with values up to 1e9

misconceptions.desc: Wrote long long x = a * b (or a + b + c + d) with int operands; overflow happens before widening.
Evaluated 2 * nums[j] (or similar) in int inside a comparison.
Assumed signed overflow wraps around predictably.

nodes.name: size_t & unsigned pitfalls
nodes.description: v.size() is unsigned; subtracting from it or counting down with size_t wraps around.

facets.explain: Knows size() returns size_t and what 0u - 1 evaluates to.
facets.implement: Stores n = (int)v.size() before arithmetic; uses int for reverse loops.

misconceptions.desc: Used v.size() - 1 in a bound; wraps to a huge value when v is empty.
Counted down with an unsigned index; i >= 0 is always true.

nodes.name: Numeric limits
nodes.description: INT_MIN / INT_MAX / LLONG_MAX (<climits>) and numeric_limits as sentinels.

facets.implement: Uses the limit matching the data type; never negates or abs()-es INT_MIN.

misconceptions.desc: Used INT_MIN/INT_MAX as a sentinel for long long data.
Negated INT_MIN or took abs(INT_MIN) (overflow).

nodes.name: Iterators & half-open ranges
nodes.description: STL ranges are [first, last); v.begin() + k points at index k.

facets.explain: Knows ranges are half-open and when iterators are invalidated.
facets.implement: Passes correct ranges, e.g. reverse(v.begin(), v.begin() + k) reverses indices 0..k-1.

misconceptions.desc: Passed begin() + k - 1 or end() - 1 as the end iterator, assuming an inclusive range.
Used an iterator after push_back/erase invalidated it.

nodes.name: STL algorithms
nodes.description: sort, reverse, swap, max/min, max_element, accumulate, rotate, unique, next_permutation, and their costs.

facets.recognize: Knows which algorithm exists for a job and its complexity (sort is O(n log n)).
facets.explain: Can implement reverse / rotate / next_permutation by hand; interviewers often forbid the library call.
facets.implement: Calls algorithms with correct arguments and uses their return values.

misconceptions.desc: accumulate(..., 0) with an int initial value overflows; needs 0LL.
Relied on std::next_permutation / rotate / unique without understanding the algorithm (fails the follow-up).
Called std::unique without using its returned iterator; size is unchanged.
Treated sort as free when the problem requires O(n).

nodes.name: unordered_map / unordered_set
nodes.description: Insertion, lookup with find/count, operator[] side effects, average O(1) cost.

facets.explain: Knows the average O(1) / worst O(n) cost, unspecified iteration order, and that operator[] inserts a default value.
facets.implement: Uses mp[key]++ for counting and find()/count() for existence checks.

misconceptions.desc: Used mp[key] to test existence, inserting key with value 0 as a side effect.
Dereferenced find() without comparing it to end().
Assumed unordered_map iterates in sorted or insertion order.

nodes.name: map / set
nodes.description: Balanced-tree containers: sorted keys, O(log n) operations, in-order iteration.

facets.explain: Knows set/map operations are O(log n), so n insertions cost O(n log n).
facets.recognize: Chooses set for sorted unique keys, multiset or a map of counts when duplicates matter.
facets.implement: Inserts, iterates in order and copies the result back to a vector.

misconceptions.desc: Treated set/map operations as O(1).
Used set where duplicate occurrences must be kept.

nodes.name: 2D vectors
nodes.description: vector<vector<int>> construction, dimensions, jagged rows, references to rows.

facets.implement: Builds mat(m, vector<int>(n, 0)), reads m = mat.size() and n = mat[0].size(), builds jagged rows, takes rows by auto&.

misconceptions.desc: Inner vectors not sized, or sized with the wrong dimension.
Took a row by value (auto row = mat[i]) and modified the copy.
